title: Functions
description: Functions, parameters, and return values in Go
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Functions

File-scope `static` helpers, prototypes, and `struct` parameters.

exercises.title: Basic Function
exercises.description: Create a function greet() that prints Hello. Call it in main.

exercises.title: Function with Parameters
exercises.description: Create function greet(name string) that prints Hello, name. Call with "Alice".

exercises.title: Function with Return
exercises.description: Create function add(a, b int) int that returns a+b. Call with 3 and 4, print result.

exercises.title: Multiple Return Values
exercises.description: Create function divide(a, b int) (int, error) that returns quotient and nil error, or 0 and error if b is 0. Call with 10 and 3, print result and error.
hints: Check if b == 0 and return errors.New("division by zero")

exercises.title: Variadic Function
exercises.description: Create function sum(numbers ...int) int that sums all numbers. Call with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and print the result.
hints: Pass pointer + length instead of variadic.

exercises.title: Defer Statement
exercises.description: Create a function process() that prints "start", defers printing "end", and prints "working". Call it in main.
hints: `atexit` registers cleanup at process exit (differs from Go defer but models cleanup).

exercises.title: Closure
exercises.description: Create function makeAdder() that returns a function that adds to a running total. Create adder := makeAdder(), then call adder(5) and adder(10), printing both results.
hints: File-scope state models the closure capture.
